---
title: "Examples"
---

A collection of examples demonstrating DeckGL.jl capabilities.

## Basic Scatterplot

Simple point visualization with data-driven sizing.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Generate sample data
n = 1000
data = (
    lng = -122.4 .+ 0.1 .* randn(n),
    lat = 37.8 .+ 0.1 .* randn(n),
    size = 50 .+ 100 .* rand(n)
)

# Create visualization
layer = ScatterplotLayer(
    data = data,
    get_position = [:lng, :lat],
    get_radius = :size,
    get_fill_color = [255, 140, 0, 180],
    radius_min_pixels = 2,
    pickable = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 11
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## Flight Routes with Arcs

Visualize connections between cities.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Sample flight routes
routes = (
    src_lng = [-122.4, -122.4, -122.4, -73.9, -87.6],
    src_lat = [37.8, 37.8, 37.8, 40.7, 41.9],
    dst_lng = [-73.9, -87.6, -118.2, -87.6, -118.2],
    dst_lat = [40.7, 41.9, 34.0, 41.9, 34.0],
    flights = [150, 80, 200, 120, 90]
)

layer = ArcLayer(
    data = routes,
    get_source_position = [:src_lng, :src_lat],
    get_target_position = [:dst_lng, :dst_lat],
    get_source_color = [0, 128, 255],
    get_target_color = [255, 0, 128],
    get_width = :flights,
    width_scale = 0.05,
    width_min_pixels = 1,
    great_circle = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -98,
        latitude = 39,
        zoom = 3,
        pitch = 30
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## GPS Tracks with Paths

Render GPS tracks or routes.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Sample paths (each path is an array of [lng, lat] coordinates)
paths_data = (
    path = [
        # Path 1: San Francisco to Oakland
        [[-122.4194, 37.7749], [-122.3, 37.8], [-122.2711, 37.8044]],
        # Path 2: Around the bay
        [[-122.4, 37.8], [-122.35, 37.85], [-122.3, 37.82], [-122.28, 37.78]]
    ],
    name = ["SF to Oakland", "Bay Loop"],
    speed = [35, 45]
)

layer = PathLayer(
    data = paths_data,
    get_path = :path,
    get_color = [0, 128, 255, 200],
    get_width = :speed,
    width_scale = 0.5,
    width_min_pixels = 2,
    cap_rounded = true,
    joint_rounded = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.35,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 11
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## Choropleth with Polygons

Colored regions based on data values.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Sample polygon data (simplified for example)
regions = (
    polygon = [
        # Region 1 (triangle)
        [[[-122.5, 37.7], [-122.4, 37.9], [-122.3, 37.7], [-122.5, 37.7]]],
        # Region 2 (quadrilateral)
        [[[-122.45, 37.75], [-122.35, 37.75], [-122.35, 37.85], [-122.45, 37.85], [-122.45, 37.75]]]
    ],
    value = [100, 200],
    name = ["Region A", "Region B"]
)

layer = PolygonLayer(
    data = regions,
    get_polygon = :polygon,
    get_fill_color = [255, 140, 0, 150],
    get_line_color = [255, 140, 0, 255],
    get_line_width = 50,
    line_width_min_pixels = 2,
    pickable = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 11
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## 3D Hexagonal Binning

Aggregate points into 3D hexagons.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Generate random earthquake-like data
n = 5000
earthquakes = (
    lng = -122.4 .+ 0.2 .* randn(n),
    lat = 37.8 .+ 0.2 .* randn(n),
    magnitude = 1 .+ 4 .* rand(n)
)

layer = HexagonLayer(
    data = earthquakes,
    get_position = [:lng, :lat],
    get_elevation_weight = :magnitude,
    radius = 500,
    elevation_scale = 50,
    elevation_range = [0, 500],
    extruded = true,
    coverage = 0.9,
    pickable = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 11,
        pitch = 45,
        bearing = 15
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## Density Heatmap

Visualize point density.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Generate clustered data
n = 10000
clusters = [
    (-122.4, 37.8, 3000),   # Downtown SF
    (-122.45, 37.75, 2000), # South
    (-122.35, 37.85, 1500)  # North
]

lng = Float64[]
lat = Float64[]
for (cx, cy, count) in clusters
    append!(lng, cx .+ 0.02 .* randn(count))
    append!(lat, cy .+ 0.02 .* randn(count))
end

data = (lng = lng, lat = lat)

layer = HeatmapLayer(
    data = data,
    get_position = [:lng, :lat],
    radius_pixels = 30,
    intensity = 1,
    threshold = 0.03
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 12
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## City Labels

Add text labels to a map.

```julia
using DeckGL

cities = (
    lng = [-122.4, -73.9, -87.6, -118.2, -95.4],
    lat = [37.8, 40.7, 41.9, 34.0, 29.8],
    name = ["San Francisco", "New York", "Chicago", "Los Angeles", "Houston"],
    population = [883305, 8336817, 2693976, 3979576, 2320268]
)

# Scatter layer for points
scatter_layer = ScatterplotLayer(
    data = cities,
    get_position = [:lng, :lat],
    get_radius = 50000,
    get_fill_color = [255, 0, 0, 200]
)

# Text layer for labels
text_layer = TextLayer(
    data = cities,
    get_position = [:lng, :lat],
    get_text = :name,
    get_size = 16,
    get_color = [0, 0, 0, 255],
    get_pixel_offset = [0, -20],
    font_family = "Arial, sans-serif"
)

deck = Deck(
    [scatter_layer, text_layer],
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -98,
        latitude = 39,
        zoom = 4
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## Multiple Layers

Combine different layer types.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Points
points = (
    lng = [-122.4, -122.45, -122.35],
    lat = [37.8, 37.75, 37.85],
    size = [200, 150, 180]
)

# Connections
connections = (
    src_lng = [-122.4, -122.4],
    src_lat = [37.8, 37.8],
    dst_lng = [-122.45, -122.35],
    dst_lat = [37.75, 37.85]
)

# Labels
labels = (
    lng = [-122.4, -122.45, -122.35],
    lat = [37.8, 37.75, 37.85],
    name = ["HQ", "Office A", "Office B"]
)

layers = [
    # Lines first (background)
    LineLayer(
        data = connections,
        get_source_position = [:src_lng, :src_lat],
        get_target_position = [:dst_lng, :dst_lat],
        get_color = [100, 100, 100, 200],
        get_width = 2
    ),
    # Points on top
    ScatterplotLayer(
        data = points,
        get_position = [:lng, :lat],
        get_radius = :size,
        get_fill_color = [0, 128, 255, 200]
    ),
    # Labels on top
    TextLayer(
        data = labels,
        get_position = [:lng, :lat],
        get_text = :name,
        get_size = 14,
        get_color = [0, 0, 0],
        get_pixel_offset = [0, -25]
    )
]

deck = Deck(
    layers,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 12
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## GeoJSON from URL

Load and display GeoJSON data from a URL.

```julia
using DeckGL

# US states GeoJSON (example URL)
layer = GeoJsonLayer(
    data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PublicaMundi/MappingAPI/master/data/geojson/us-states.json",
    filled = true,
    stroked = true,
    get_fill_color = [200, 200, 255, 100],
    get_line_color = [0, 0, 128, 255],
    get_line_width = 2,
    line_width_min_pixels = 1,
    pickable = true
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -98,
        latitude = 39,
        zoom = 4
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```

## Using Convenience Functions

Quick visualizations with minimal code.

```julia
using DeckGL

# Generate data
n = 1000
data = (
    lng = -122.4 .+ 0.1 .* randn(n),
    lat = 37.8 .+ 0.1 .* randn(n),
    value = rand(n) .* 100
)

# One-liner visualizations
scatter(data, :lng, :lat, radius=:value, color=[255, 0, 0]) |> open_html

heatmap(data, :lng, :lat, weight=:value) |> open_html

hexbin(data, :lng, :lat, elevation_weight=:value, radius=300) |> open_html
```

## Working with DataFrames

DeckGL.jl works seamlessly with DataFrames.

```julia
using DeckGL
using DataFrames

# Create a DataFrame
df = DataFrame(
    longitude = [-122.4, -122.5, -122.3, -122.45],
    latitude = [37.8, 37.7, 37.9, 37.75],
    category = ["A", "B", "A", "B"],
    value = [100, 200, 150, 180]
)

# Use DataFrame directly
layer = ScatterplotLayer(
    data = df,
    get_position = [:longitude, :latitude],
    get_radius = :value,
    get_fill_color = [255, 140, 0, 200]
)

deck = Deck(
    layer,
    initial_view_state = ViewState(
        longitude = -122.4,
        latitude = 37.8,
        zoom = 11
    )
)

open_html(deck)
```
